title: Monte Carlo simulation of the switching curve
action: Implement a Monte Carlo simulation of a 2D antiferromagnetic Ising model on a 1000×1000 square lattice with nearest‑neighbour exchange J = −1 and periodic boundary conditions. Initialize the spins antiferromagnetically. For each reduced temperature t = 0.02, 0.03, …, 0.20 (or a finer grid), thermalise for ~1000 Monte Carlo steps, then apply a spatially oscillating magnetic field (+h, −h) on the two sublattices. Scan h and record the critical switching field where the net magnetisation changes sign. Save the (t, h) pairs as `/app/outputs/switching_curve.csv`.
description: Raw switching curve data (t, h) produced by the Monte Carlo simulation.

title: Extract temperature regimes from switching curve
action: From the switching curve data in `/app/outputs/switching_curve.csv`, identify the low‑temperature region, the flat plateau region, and the high‑temperature decrease. Determine the temperature t1 at which the plateau begins, t2 at which it ends, and the average switching field h_plateau on the plateau. Write these three values to `/app/outputs/regimes.json` with keys `t1`, `t2`, `h_plateau`.
description: Scored artifact containing the extracted temperature regime boundaries and plateau height.
